answer: Coordination-Density Pairing. Agents that jointly act must submit a shared coordination kernel: a signed transcript of their prior pairwise interactions. The system prices admission by the density of that kernel — sparse graphs (few dense prior exchanges) are charged sharply more per member. Sybil clusters produce hollow transcripts, so each fake identity pays the sparse-graph rate rather than the pooled rate. Any echo of an existing cluster's transcript is flagged and rerated upward. Attacker cost: near-linear payment per added identity, and repeated transcript reuse triggers escalating fees.
